I have a tendency to believe that most people feel like they need to fit in somewhere, into some label, in order to have an identity. I recently was dicussing this with my friend who had a mini identity crisis and didn't know who he was or what he liked. He would just work 60 hours a week, go home and wait to die or to wake up for work again.

I reflected in this and decided that people should just do what they find fun or interesting. If they don't fit in anywhere, they will fit in anywhere.

If I use myself as an example: I have been riding motorcycles since I was a teenager, about 18 years now. I enjoy working on them also and did so professionally throughout high school and a few years after. This allows me to strike up conversation with motorcycle people and talk about bikes.

I am a pipe tradesman, specifically heating and cooling. I find myself with lots of things to talk about with fitters, plumbers and techs so we can talk shop and have a great time.

I service my own vehicles, but specifically I own a Mercedes and used to own a BMW. This allows me to get into the auto service crowd as well as german auto enthusiasts.

As part of my job I do building automation service which involves custom logic programming, networking, and system troubleshooting. This gives me an opportunity to strike up conversation with IT professionals to learn and discuss.

I have been a gamer since the days of Doom on DOS and always enjoyed tinkering with computers, tweaking configs for drivers, and building my own rigs. I have a small collection computers, laptops, netbooks running windows, macOS, and different flavors of Linux. I am always messing with them, doing little projects, whatever suits my fancy, just to learn more and be more well versed in the subject. So now I have an avenue to talk with PC gamers, PC builders, anyone in the cult of mac, and can also learn from Linux power users.

Finally I save my old console gaming systems so in the rare occasion I encounter a retro gamer we can chat about that too.

So depending on the group and how they see me first I am a computer nerd, gamer tard, tradesman, handyman, pretentious Mercedes owner, mechanic etc. People always feel the need to put other people in a category.

If anyone asked me though, I'd say I am a dad and a husband. That's really who I am. Without my family I am just a guy trying to keep busy.

I still stand by my point though and let others choose a label, its up to you to accept it or not, but if someone wants to call me something other than my name I'm generally ok with it.
